title: Incline Barbell Bench Press
summary: Barbell bench press on a 30-45 degree incline: chest 1 with upper chest 1, front delts 0.6, triceps 0.5.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights); adjustable (incline) bench.

muscles.why: Pressing on an incline lines up with the upper chest; upper 1, mid/lower 0.7.

region_notes.text: Incline pressing grew the upper chest more than flat pressing in one 8-week study in untrained men.

muscles.why: More shoulder flexion than flat, so the front delts help more.
The triceps lock out the bar.

setup.text: Bench at 30-45 degrees, bar in the rack hooks.
Grip a little wider than shoulders; shoulder blades back.
Unrack with a spotter if near failure.

form_cues.cue: Lower the bar to your upper chest
form_cues.why: Lowering to the upper chest lines the bar up with the upper pec.

form_cues.cue: Keep shoulder blades pinned to the bench
Press straight up over the shoulders
form_cues.why: A small arch with the shoulder blades back keeps the shoulders steady.

bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps more of the work on the chest.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Setting the bench so steep the lift turns into a shoulder press.
mistakes.fix: Set the shoulder blades back before you unrack.

misconceptions.myth: Flat bench doesn't work the upper chest.
Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: Ramp up before your first working set. For primary lifts the app suggests 50% x 8, 70% x 4 and 85% x 2 when the first working load is 60 kg or more, and 50% x 8 then 75% x 3 below that.
lower_risk.note: High-load warm-ups improved strength performance in a systematic review; the percentages are coaching convention.

lower_risk.text: Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 6-10 rep range. Keep heavy sets a few reps short of failure without a spotter.
Bench with a spotter or with safety arms set just above chest height. With no safeties or spotter, leave collars off so plates can be tipped off a stuck bar.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Same incline with dumbbells: more stretch.

notes: The upper-chest finding is one 8-week study in untrained men.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
